KEY MESSAGE 1...Low pressure developing well off the North 
Carolina coast tonight will deepen and move north towards New 
England this weekend. 

Low pressure developing well off the North Carolina coast tonight 
will deepen and move north towards New England this weekend. 

Strong high pressure remains in place across eastern Canada this 
evening and it will hold fast into Thursday before slowly 
diminishing. Meanwhile, low pressure is organizing well offshore of 
the North Carolina coast and it will further deepen and track 
northward Thursday through Saturday. The exact track that this low 
is still somewhat uncertain, but now overall looks to remain far 
enough offshore to keep heavy rains away from the region. Still, the 
strengthening pressure gradient between the low and departing high 
will create increasing NorthEast winds across our region tonight and 
into the end of the week. We'll continue with the Wind Advisory for 
the coastal areas attm. Gusts of 45 to 50 mph are expected at times. 

The main impacts of the approaching storm look to be Marine and 
Coastal-land with tidal flooding and strong gusty winds along the 
shore areas. Inland winds will be gusty as well (mostly 20 to 30 
mph). We highlight the latest thinking with the surf and coastal 
flooding in the Key Messages below. 

Rain chances are near zero for all areas tonight, slight chance for 
coastal Delaware and south NJ for Thursday and then just chance (30%-
50%) for shore areas Thursday night and Friday. Slight chance pops 
are in there for Thursday night and Friday for the remainder of 
NJ/DE and eastern PA too. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Multiple rounds of significant tidal flooding 
expected into this weekend. Coastal Flood Warnings and 
Advisories remain in effect.

With a slow moving coastal storm and multiple days of strong 
northeast winds expected, the confidence in the threat for tidal 
flooding remains high. Strong onshore flow that is projected to last 
for several days will result in water piling up across tidal 
tributaries and within back bays of coastal communities. Tidal 
levels will also be enhanced with astronomical tides increasing with 
the upcoming Full Moon on Saturday. This combination of factors will 
lead to widespread tidal flooding, some of which will get well into 
Moderate stage. While not currently forecast, the threat for Major 
flooding is not off the table, especially getting near the full 
moon. Tidal guidance diverges greatly beyond Thursday Night at 
nearly all of our forecast points. Some guidance has moderate to 
even major flooding for the weekend while some barely has tide 
levels getting into minor flood stage. It all will depend on the 
track of the coastal storm. 

No significant changes were made to the Coastal Flood Warnings and 
Advisories that are in effect through Friday evening. However, 
Warnings and/or Advisories may have to be extended into Saturday 
depending on the exact track and strength of the low.

For the tidal Delaware River, tide levels are expected to reach 
widespread minor today and Thursday. Coastal Flood Advisories remain 
in effect for the tidal Delaware River through Thursday night's high 
tide. As with the areas mentioned above, widespread minor tidal 
flooding may continue through Friday and into the weekend.

Usually, strong northeast winds do not result in tidal flooding
along the upper Eastern Shore of Maryland. However, given the 
duration of surge in the lower/southern portion of the bay with 
widespread moderate to major flooding forecast there, it is 
becoming increasingly likely that portions of our Eastern Shore 
counties will experience some minor tidal flooding toward the 
end of the week. Our latest forecast includes Claiborne reaching
minor flood stage for 4 consecutive high tides beginning with 
tonight's high tide. Thus, a Coastal Flood Advisory was issued 
for Queen Anne's Talbot, and Caroline Counties. Our latest 
forecast has also increased slightly for Tolchester Beach, and 
and expansion to Kent (MD) County may be considered in a future
update depending on how surge values trend. By Friday and 
Saturday, winds shifting more northerly should help the bay to 
begin draining some.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Dangerous rip currents and high surf are 
expected at the Jersey Shore and Delaware Beaches through the 
end of the week. Beach erosion is likely and spotty dune erosion
is possible.

A coastal storm developing offshore will result in hazardous 
conditions along the coast. The surface low will linger off our 
coast for multiple days, bringing strong northeast winds and 
high seas for our marine zones. Breaking waves within the surf 
zone of 6 to 12 feet are expected through Saturday. Dangerous 
rip currents will accompany the high surf, making it extremely 
dangerous to enter the water at any time through Saturday. The 
high surf and strong winds could also result in beach erosion
